government.short_title: Anti-Corruption Efforts and Citizen-Initiated Accountability: Evidence from Administrative Lit…
government.source: Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how when leaders are punished for corruption, it affects citizens' willingness to challenge the government through formal channels. It found that if provincial leaders get convicted of corruption, more citizens start taking action by filing lawsuits against the government. This effect is stronger when there are better ways to handle these cases in court. However, this doesn't happen as much when the area has a lot of corruption problems.

government.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
government.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

government.title: The Role of Government Structure in the Emergence of Crimes Against Humanity
government.short_title: The Role of Government Structure in the Emergence of Crimes Against Humanity
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: The study found that certain government structures can facilitate crimes against humanity by concentrating power in authoritarian regimes, allowing discriminatory ideologies to dominate, causing crises in legitimacy, or implementing unfair economic policies. These factors weaken checks on violence, legitimize harmful actions, suppress opposition groups, and cause harm to specific populations. To prevent such crimes, it's important for governments to strengthen the rule of law, ensure judicial independence, expand democratic oversight, and promote human rights values within their systems.

government.title: An Examination of Government Methods for Compensating Damage Resulting from Infringement of Public Rights
government.short_title: An Examination of Government Methods for Compensating Damage Resulting from Infringement of Pu…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how governments in Iran handle situations where their actions harm collective interests or public rights. It examines legal systems that provide ways to compensate for such harms and restore balance. The research finds there are different types of compensation depending on whether the government acted wrongfully or not, and it also covers cases where they did something lawful but still caused damage. Challenges like unclear laws, difficulty proving harm in collective situations, and lack of coordination between different parts of the system can make these mechanisms less effective even if the basic rules are clear.

government.title: The Dual Impact of International Sanctions and FATF Requirements on the Independence and Effectiveness of Government Financial Supervision in Iran’s Public Law System
government.short_title: The Dual Impact of International Sanctions and FATF Requirements on the Independence and Effec…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: Financial supervision in Iran faces significant challenges due to both international sanctions and FATF requirements. These pressures affect how government institutions manage resources and ensure transparency. Sanctions limit access to data and cooperation with other countries, while FATF standards promote more formal procedures for oversight but also increase compliance costs. This creates a complex environment where institutions can gain technical tools but lose their independence due to external constraints like sanctions.

government.title: A Qualitative Analysis of Administrative Transparency Requirements in Government Construction Contracts with Emphasis on the Jurisprudence of the Administrative Court of Justice and Data-Driven Governance
government.short_title: A Qualitative Analysis of Administrative Transparency Requirements in Government Construction…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how governments should make their construction contract processes more transparent to prevent inefficiencies and corruption. It covers all stages from deciding what to build to evaluating its success. Transparency isn't just about sharing information; it also means having clear rules, fair procedures, and being able to prove decisions were right. The court's rulings on this matter help enforce transparency as a legal requirement.

government.short_title: Evaluation of the Policymaking System and Institutions for Combating Administrative Corruption…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: During the Republican period in Afghanistan (2004-2021), administrative corruption was a major issue affecting governance. The government worked with international support to create laws, anti-corruption strategies, and institutions. However, despite progress in these areas, corruption did not significantly decrease. The study found that while there were improvements in legislation and institution building, the effectiveness of policies weakened at implementation stages.

government.title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
government.short_title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Inte…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: This research evaluates Iran's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to see how well it supports responsible use of AI. The strategy emphasizes values like human dignity and national priorities, but lacks clear plans for key areas like funding, data access, and regulation. To succeed, the strategy needs more specific details on these aspects. Practitioners should focus not just on ethical principles, but also on practical steps to ensure AI is used responsibly and effectively in Iran.

government.title: Digital innovation for strategic decision-making in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs: integrating ERP systems, data analytics, and digital governance
government.short_title: Digital innovation for strategic decision-making in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs: integrati…
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how the Ministry of Foreign Affairs used digital innovations like integrating ERP systems, data analytics tools, and improving digital governance to make better decisions. By doing this, they improved their operations, made decisions faster and smarter, and increased transparency in their work. The study suggests a way to use these technologies together for better overall management and decision-making that benefits the public.

government.title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental, Philippines
government.short_title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental…
government.plain_summary: This research highlights that while investing in mangrove restoration in Davao Occidental has been significant, outcomes have varied widely due to issues like incorrect species selection and lack of monitoring. Studies show that by matching the right species to each site and diversifying plant types, survival rates can be very high at over 95%. However, these effective methods are not consistently used because there's no unified policy framework. The study suggests creating a standardized governance system that mandates correct species use, promotes diverse planting strategies, and establishes community monitoring systems supported by partnerships between local governments and universities.

government.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
government.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
government.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
government.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

government.title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary After Indonesian Constitutional Court Decision No. 66/PUU-XXIV/2026: A Fiqh Siyasah Perspective
government.short_title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary…
government.source: JISRev: Journal of Islamic Studies Review
government.plain_summary: This research looks at the difference between maladministration and corruption, using a specific case about buying Chromebooks for schools in Indonesia. It found four key factors to decide if something is corruption: whether someone intended to do wrong, if they got personal benefit from it, if money was lost as a result, and if proper steps were taken afterward. The study also suggests that when all these factors are met, what started as maladministration can be considered corruption. However, the research points out there should be an initial check by a special committee before going to criminal courts.

government.short_title: The Role of Ethics in the Implementation of Anti-Corruption Standards for Civil Servants in Ru…
government.source: Public International and Private International Law
government.plain_summary: Corruption damages trust in government by civil servants. To fight it effectively, we need strong ethical standards alongside institutional changes. Russia and China have taken different approaches to this; studying their methods can help create better systems globally. Understanding both universal principles and cultural specifics is key for creating effective anti-corruption measures.

government.title: Combating Corruption in the Migration Sector: The History and the Present Time
government.short_title: Combating Corruption in the Migration Sector: The History and the Present Time
government.plain_summary: Corruption is widespread in the migration sector, posing significant risks to national security and foreign policy. In Russia, there has been an increase in migration-related crimes, which exposes this area to corruption risks. To combat these issues, it's important to strengthen laws and regulations related to migration, ensuring they are effective against corruption. This can help protect citizens from exploitation and reduce the risk of international conflicts over migration policies.

government.title: The Role of Digital Technologies in Minimizing the Causes and Conditions of Corruption
government.short_title: The Role of Digital Technologies in Minimizing the Causes and Conditions of Corruption
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how digital technologies like AI, blockchain, and open data can help reduce corruption in government work. It shows that using these tools effectively depends on having good rules, strong leaders who want to fight corruption, and proper laws protecting information. While technology alone isn't a magic solution, it's seen as part of a bigger plan to stop corrupt practices.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.short_title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.plain_summary: Data science has become crucial as we generate vast amounts of information daily. It helps transform this data into useful insights for better decision-making across various sectors. For audit institutions, integrating data science can enhance their ability to manage public funds more effectively and improve accountability. By using data science, audits can provide clearer and more accurate reports that recommend improvements faster, which benefits the overall administration and improves citizens' quality of life.

government.title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.short_title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses a scenario where autonomous killer robots are used in warfare without human intervention. These robots can make decisions about who to target based on AI algorithms trained to recognize certain uniforms. If one of these drones targets and kills an enemy soldier who is surrendering, it would violate international laws. Another concern is if the robot makes a mistake by attacking another similar system, leading to unintended conflicts.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.short_title: Collaborative Governance in Palm Oil Permit Enforcement: Anti-Corruption Supervision, Indigeno…
government.source: Journal of Business, Social and Technology
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how different groups work together in West Papua to manage palm oil plantations properly. It found that the Corruption Eradication Commission, civil society organizations, and experts all played important roles in making sure licenses were fair and didn't lead to corruption. The KPK helped make sure everyone was following rules. EcoNusa and other experts provided legal and social support.

government.short_title: Pedagogy of Anti-Corruption Education: Conceptual Foundations and Implementation Tools
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how to teach students about avoiding corruption through courses like "Legal Foundations of Professional Activity." It explains the basic ideas behind teaching people not to be corrupt and suggests ways to make students dislike corruption. The goal is to help create a society where people don't accept or do corrupt things. To achieve this, it teaches students about what corruption is and how to fight it legally. It also helps them understand good values like honesty and fairness so they won’t want to be corrupt.

government.title: Strategi Komunikasi dan Relationship Marketing dalam Meningkatkan Kepercayaan Publik pada Lembaga Nonprofit: Studi Kasus Dompet Dhuafa
government.short_title: Strategi Komunikasi dan Relationship Marketing dalam Meningkatkan Kepercayaan Publik pada Lemb…
government.source: Comit: Communication, Information and Technology Journal
government.plain_summary: Nonprofit organizations like Dompet Dhuafa in Indonesia play a crucial role in supporting social development through various programs. To build public trust effectively, they need not only to collect funds but also use strategic communication methods and relationship marketing. This study found that digital communication strategies, transparency in reports, and emotional connection-building are key factors for increasing donor loyalty and public participation. Dompet Dhuafa uses social media, campaigns, and storytelling to enhance its image and build strong relationships with the public.

government.title: The burden of bribery: How bank credit constraints mediate the relationship between corruption and trade credit in private firms
government.short_title: The burden of bribery: How bank credit constraints mediate the relationship between corruption…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how corruption impacts private firms' use of trade credit and whether access to formal bank financing influences this relationship. Using data from 60,732 manufacturing firms across 130 countries, it found that when corruption affects the formal banking system, firms tend to rely more on supplier financing as a financial safety net. Specifically, firms exposed to corruption finance about 1.32 percentage points more of their working capital through trade credit, which is roughly equivalent to $13,200 per million dollars in working capital. This effect is stronger for firms without access to bank lines or loans.

government.title: Anti-Corruption Law in Vietnam : Limitations in Design and Implementation, Orientations for Improving the Legal System
government.short_title: Anti-Corruption Law in Vietnam : Limitations in Design and Implementation, Orientations for Im…
government.source: Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
government.plain_summary: Anti-corruption laws in Vietnam have been established but their enforcement is not as strong as expected. While there are some formal measures like requiring officials to disclose income and assets, these are often seen through a lens of formality rather than substance. There's also a lack of clear guidelines for preventing conflicts of interest among public servants. Additionally, protecting those who report corruption effectively isn't well-enforced, and recovering stolen funds is limited.

government.title: 40 Years of Corruption Research in China: Theory, Evidence, and Future Directions
government.short_title: 40 Years of Corruption Research in China: Theory, Evidence, and Future Directions
government.plain_summary: This review covers 40 years of corruption studies conducted by Chinese researchers. It looks at how corruption affects governance and government legitimacy in China since reforms began in 1978. Scholars have developed their own theories, incorporating cultural aspects specific to China's centralized political environment. They've also explored strategies for combating corruption, which differs from Western approaches.

government.title: A framework for AI readiness and strategic adoption: developing a public sector AI maturity model through systematic review and synthesis
government.short_title: A framework for AI readiness and strategic adoption: developing a public sector AI maturity mo…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study aims to help public sector organizations understand and adopt artificial intelligence effectively. It found that factors like leadership, governance, transparency, and ethical oversight are crucial for successful AI use in government. The research proposes a five-level maturity model showing how an organization can progress from using AI sporadically to integrating it into daily operations in a responsible way. This framework helps public sector leaders plan their AI journey systematically.

government.title: The Communalization of Law Enforcement in India: Police Complicity, Impunity, and Anti-Muslim Violence
government.short_title: The Communalization of Law Enforcement in India: Police Complicity, Impunity, and Anti-Muslim…
government.source: Tebuireng: Journal of Islamic Studies and Society
government.plain_summary: This research examines how Indian police can become involved in anti-Muslim riots through various means like delayed responses or selective enforcement. It looks at three specific incidents of violence: one in Gujarat in 2002, another in Muzaffarnagar in 2013, and a third in Northeast Delhi in 2020. The study finds common patterns such as police not intervening quickly enough, enforcing laws unevenly, conducting biased investigations after the fact, and failing to hold perpetrators accountable. By using theories from experts like Paul Brass, Veena Das, Michel Foucault, and Deana Heath, it explains why these issues persist in different political situations and places.

government.title: Regulatory Path of "Data-Driven Price Discrimination" from the Perspective of Anti-unfair Competition Law
government.short_title: Regulatory Path of "Data-Driven Price Discrimination" from the Perspective of Anti-unfair Comp…
government.source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
government.plain_summary: In recent years, businesses have started using big data to offer different prices based on customer information. This practice is seen as unfair by many because it benefits some customers over others without a fair reason. Currently, China doesn't have specific laws about this issue, so existing anti-unfair competition rules are weak in areas like enforcement and proof of unfairness. By studying cases and comparing with other countries' experiences, we can develop new regulations that cover how to classify such behavior, make algorithms more transparent, provide better protections for consumers, encourage cooperation between different industries, and strengthen regulatory oversight.

government.title: Structured prioritization of stakeholder preferences in digital governance: a comparative AHP framework for public-sector decision alignment
government.short_title: Structured prioritization of stakeholder preferences in digital governance: a comparative AHP…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses how to better align digital governance decisions by understanding what different stakeholders value. It uses a framework called AHP, which helps identify the most important goals for improving things like quality of life, sustainability, innovation, and competitiveness in cities. By comparing these priorities across various groups, including public officials and citizens, we can see where there might be disagreements or gaps in how policies are made. This model allows city planners to make decisions that better reflect what people want and expect from their government.

government.title: Anti-Monopoly Legal Compliance Risks in the Pharmaceutical Industry
government.short_title: Anti-Monopoly Legal Compliance Risks in the Pharmaceutical Industry
government.source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
government.plain_summary: In the pharmaceutical industry, there are risks related to monopolistic practices when dealing with raw materials like APIs. These include barriers to entry that can lead to passive collusion, new types of cartels using modern technology, and changes in how governments enforce antitrust laws. To address these issues, companies need to implement three main compliance mechanisms: early warning systems for pricing, digital audits within the company, and comprehensive risk management for all employees. This helps prevent illegal activities and ensures that companies comply with anti-monopoly regulations.

government.title: Modern Anti-Corruption Policy in the USA, EU, and Ukraine: Medico-Pharmaceutical Law as the Basic of Forensic Pharmaceutical and Criminal Research on the Exclusion of Criminal Actions in Healthcare Institutions
government.short_title: Modern Anti-Corruption Policy in the USA, EU, and Ukraine: Medico-Pharmaceutical Law as the Ba…
government.source: SSP Modern Economics, State and Public Administration
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how corruption affects healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors in Europe and Ukraine. It highlights that corruption is widespread, appearing both openly (like bribery) and secretly (like favoritism). The study suggests focusing more on preventing corruption rather than just catching people who do it. To prevent this, educational programs for doctors and pharmacists should be strengthened, along with cooperation between different government agencies.

government.title: The Effectiveness of Official Development Assistance Within Human Security Framework: A Focus on the Role of Corruption
government.short_title: The Effectiveness of Official Development Assistance Within Human Security Framework: A Focus…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how Official Development Assistance (ODA) can help improve different aspects of human security. It found that ODA is more effective in improving health issues but less so for broader structural problems like corruption or political instability. The level of corruption also plays a big role; where there's better control over corruption, ODA tends to work better across all areas of human security. So, while aid can be helpful, it needs to be used carefully and effectively to make the most impact in places with lower levels of corruption.

government.title: Epistemic Marginalisation in the Fight Against Systemic Corruption: Explaining the Anti‐Corruption Design‐Reality Gap in South Africa
government.short_title: Epistemic Marginalisation in the Fight Against Systemic Corruption: Explaining the Anti‐Corrup…
government.plain_summary: The study found that anti-corruption reforms often don't match the realities on the ground, especially in countries like South Africa. Researchers looked at how local people's views differ from what was included in a national strategy aimed at fighting corruption. They discovered there is a big difference between what experts think should be done and what actually gets implemented. Local people see corruption as deeply rooted in society’s norms and practices, while the strategy focuses more on traditional ideas about government control over corruption.

government.title: Technologization of Anti-Corruption Policy and Changes in the Procedure for income control
government.short_title: Technologization of Anti-Corruption Policy and Changes in the Procedure for income control
government.plain_summary: Anti-corruption policies aim to prevent corruption by identifying individuals who might be involved. In Russia, this has changed from annual reports filled out manually to focusing on specific areas like personnel decisions and property transactions. Now, there's a digital platform that monitors these activities in real-time using objective data from various sources. This helps catch any discrepancies or hidden assets quickly.

government.title: Bibliometric Analysis of Blockchain for E-Government: Historical Institutionalism and Governance of Secure Digital Identity in Public Sector Services
government.short_title: Bibliometric Analysis of Blockchain for E-Government: Historical Institutionalism and Governan…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how blockchain technology is used in government services like e-government systems that handle digital IDs securely. It found that while many studies focus on the technical benefits of blockchain like security and efficiency, less attention has been given to why governments adopt these technologies. The study analyzed over 1700 documents from 2000 to 2025 and used a method called bibliometric analysis to understand how research trends have developed. It shows that since around 2017, more people are studying blockchain in government services.

government.title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.short_title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.plain_summary: Political corruption is a big problem that governments often struggle with and sometimes use anti-corruption measures against their own democracy. International Anti-Corruption Commissions (IACCs) help address this issue by working with both international experts and local people. Some IACCs have more independence than others, which can affect how effective they are in fighting corruption. In places like northern Central America, when there are coalitions that include government insiders and activists at the table during negotiations, these groups use their influence to make sure anti-corruption efforts don't undermine democracy too much.

government.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Transparency, and Public Service Delivery
government.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Tran…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how artificial intelligence is being used in government services. It found that while AI can speed up service delivery and improve monitoring of processes, it also creates issues like unclear responsibility for decisions made by AI systems, lack of transparency about these decisions, uneven readiness among staff to use AI, and risks to human decision-making. To address these challenges, the study recommends creating clear guidelines on accountability, making AI explanations transparent, encouraging public disclosure, ensuring human oversight over AI processes, providing training for staff, and offering ways for citizens to appeal if they have concerns about AI decisions.

government.title: Valuation Methods for Assessing Government-Owned Heritage Buildings in Malaysia
government.short_title: Valuation Methods for Assessing Government-Owned Heritage Buildings in Malaysia
government.source: IPN Journal of Research and Practice in Public Sector Accounting and Management
government.plain_summary: This study aimed to find suitable methods for valuing government-owned historic buildings in Malaysia. It used focus group discussions with experts from various fields like architecture and conservation. The research concluded that these buildings should be valued using a cost approach, focusing on their reproduction costs rather than assigning them a low value of RM1. This ensures compliance with the Malaysian Public Sector Accounting Standards (MPSAS).

government.title: From Corruption to Declining Public Trust: Implications for Political Participation in West Aceh Regency
government.short_title: From Corruption to Declining Public Trust: Implications for Political Participation in West Ac…
government.plain_summary: Corruption significantly impacts the level of public trust in West Aceh Regency's governance, affecting both elected and non-elected institutions. Citizens view corruption as a lack of accountability and transparency, using public resources unfairly. This perception leads to declining trust in government bodies. To improve this situation, it’s important to strengthen formal accountability, transparency, and oversight mechanisms.

government.title: Public Procurement's Long COVID : Emergency Responses and Shifting Corruption Risks in Europe
government.short_title: Public Procurement's Long COVID : Emergency Responses and Shifting Corruption Risks in Europe
government.plain_summary: This study examines how the public procurement system in Europe was affected during the pandemic. It found that spending on coronavirus-related projects led to an increase in corruption risks, especially in countries where government controls are not very strict. This happened because new companies without experience dealing with COVID-19 products took advantage of weak regulations to win big contracts. The study also noted that this increased risk spread beyond just healthcare procurement into other areas like general public services.

government.title: Methodology for assessing the impact of integration diplomacy on transparency, accountability and the effectiveness of public administration in small states
government.short_title: Methodology for assessing the impact of integration diplomacy on transparency, accountability…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how joining international groups can improve how a country runs its government. It uses Kyrgyzstan as an example and found that when countries join these groups, they often see improvements in things like transparency and efficiency. However, it also noted that just being part of these groups isn't enough to make big changes; other reforms within the country are needed too. The study suggests that while joining international groups can help, it doesn’t automatically fix all problems with government work.

nonprofit.title: The Ethics of Islamic Philanthropy
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study about Islamic philanthropy uses Quranic teachings to understand the ethics behind giving. It identifies four key principles: being responsible (amanah), improving oneself (tazkiyah), sharing with others in cycles (dawr), and giving back as a way of receiving (mukāfa’ah). These principles form a strong moral foundation for Islamic charity, showing it's not just about voluntary acts but also includes duties. This research helps clarify how these ethical guidelines affect the structure and diversity within nonprofit organizations.

nonprofit.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

nonprofit.title: The New Middle Class of Iran and the Demand for Reforming Domestic and Foreign Political Relations
nonprofit.short_title: The New Middle Class of Iran and the Demand for Reforming Domestic and Foreign Political Relat…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
nonprofit.plain_summary: The new middle class in Iran grew significantly after the Islamic Revolution and played a key role in pushing for reforms in both domestic and foreign policies. This group became more active in elections over time, aiming to influence how the government handled these areas. Despite their efforts through voting, they haven't been able to fully change the system's approach to politics internationally or domestically. Their success was mainly seen in getting more people involved in electoral processes.

nonprofit.title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
nonprofit.short_title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Inte…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research evaluates Iran's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to see how well it supports responsible use of AI. The strategy emphasizes values like human dignity and national priorities, but lacks clear plans for key areas like funding, data access, and regulation. To succeed, the strategy needs more specific details on these aspects. Practitioners should focus not just on ethical principles, but also on practical steps to ensure AI is used responsibly and effectively in Iran.

nonprofit.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
nonprofit.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
nonprofit.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
nonprofit.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

nonprofit.title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary After Indonesian Constitutional Court Decision No. 66/PUU-XXIV/2026: A Fiqh Siyasah Perspective
nonprofit.short_title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary…
nonprofit.source: JISRev: Journal of Islamic Studies Review
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research looks at the difference between maladministration and corruption, using a specific case about buying Chromebooks for schools in Indonesia. It found four key factors to decide if something is corruption: whether someone intended to do wrong, if they got personal benefit from it, if money was lost as a result, and if proper steps were taken afterward. The study also suggests that when all these factors are met, what started as maladministration can be considered corruption. However, the research points out there should be an initial check by a special committee before going to criminal courts.

nonprofit.title: Collaborative Governance in Palm Oil Permit Enforcement: Anti-Corruption Supervision, Indigenous Rights, and Sustainable Development in West Papua
nonprofit.short_title: Collaborative Governance in Palm Oil Permit Enforcement: Anti-Corruption Supervision, Indigeno…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Business, Social and Technology
nonprofit.plain_summary: This article looks at how different groups work together in West Papua to manage palm oil plantations properly. It found that the Corruption Eradication Commission, civil society organizations, and experts all played important roles in making sure licenses were fair and didn't lead to corruption. The KPK helped make sure everyone was following rules. EcoNusa and other experts provided legal and social support.

nonprofit.title: Application of the balanced scorecard (BSC) model in performance management of nonprofit organizations: the case of UNICEF<b></b>
nonprofit.short_title: Application of the balanced scorecard (BSC) model in performance management of nonprofit organ…
nonprofit.plain_summary: Nonprofit organizations are looking for ways to measure their success more effectively, especially since they aim to achieve social goals. The Balanced Scorecard (BSC) is one tool that helps them do this by using both financial and non-financial measures. A study looked at how well UNICEF uses the BSC in its performance management system. They found that when organizations use their indicators correctly and understand their strategies, it leads to better monitoring of their progress.

nonprofit.title: Strategi Komunikasi dan Relationship Marketing dalam Meningkatkan Kepercayaan Publik pada Lembaga Nonprofit: Studi Kasus Dompet Dhuafa
nonprofit.short_title: Strategi Komunikasi dan Relationship Marketing dalam Meningkatkan Kepercayaan Publik pada Lemb…
nonprofit.source: Comit: Communication, Information and Technology Journal
nonprofit.plain_summary: Nonprofit organizations like Dompet Dhuafa in Indonesia play a crucial role in supporting social development through various programs. To build public trust effectively, they need not only to collect funds but also use strategic communication methods and relationship marketing. This study found that digital communication strategies, transparency in reports, and emotional connection-building are key factors for increasing donor loyalty and public participation. Dompet Dhuafa uses social media, campaigns, and storytelling to enhance its image and build strong relationships with the public.

nonprofit.title: 40 Years of Corruption Research in China: Theory, Evidence, and Future Directions
nonprofit.short_title: 40 Years of Corruption Research in China: Theory, Evidence, and Future Directions
nonprofit.plain_summary: This review covers 40 years of corruption studies conducted by Chinese researchers. It looks at how corruption affects governance and government legitimacy in China since reforms began in 1978. Scholars have developed their own theories, incorporating cultural aspects specific to China's centralized political environment. They've also explored strategies for combating corruption, which differs from Western approaches.

nonprofit.title: Regulatory Path of "Data-Driven Price Discrimination" from the Perspective of Anti-unfair Competition Law
nonprofit.short_title: Regulatory Path of "Data-Driven Price Discrimination" from the Perspective of Anti-unfair Comp…
nonprofit.source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
nonprofit.plain_summary: In recent years, businesses have started using big data to offer different prices based on customer information. This practice is seen as unfair by many because it benefits some customers over others without a fair reason. Currently, China doesn't have specific laws about this issue, so existing anti-unfair competition rules are weak in areas like enforcement and proof of unfairness. By studying cases and comparing with other countries' experiences, we can develop new regulations that cover how to classify such behavior, make algorithms more transparent, provide better protections for consumers, encourage cooperation between different industries, and strengthen regulatory oversight.

nonprofit.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Transparency, and Public Service Delivery
nonprofit.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Tran…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research looks at how artificial intelligence is being used in government services. It found that while AI can speed up service delivery and improve monitoring of processes, it also creates issues like unclear responsibility for decisions made by AI systems, lack of transparency about these decisions, uneven readiness among staff to use AI, and risks to human decision-making. To address these challenges, the study recommends creating clear guidelines on accountability, making AI explanations transparent, encouraging public disclosure, ensuring human oversight over AI processes, providing training for staff, and offering ways for citizens to appeal if they have concerns about AI decisions.

nonprofit.title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
nonprofit.short_title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
nonprofit.source: Journal of Social Politics and Governance (JSPG)
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how different groups like governments, businesses, non-profits, schools, and media work together to fight corruption using something called the Pentahelix framework. It found that for effective anti-corruption efforts, these groups need to collaborate closely rather than working separately. The Pentahelix model shows they can tackle corruption more effectively when they all play a part in it. This collaborative approach is key to creating strong systems against corruption and making sure it doesn't happen anymore.

nonprofit.title: Bureaucratic Ethics and Organizational Integrity: The Challenges of Anti-Corruption Culture in Apparatus Behavior
nonprofit.short_title: Bureaucratic Ethics and Organizational Integrity: The Challenges of Anti-Corruption Culture in…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Governance and Local Politics (JGLP)
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research looks at how ethical values are practiced in government organizations to prevent corruption. It highlights a gap between what laws say and how people actually behave in their work. To fix this, it suggests that improving individual ethics and creating an environment where transparency is valued more can help. The biggest hurdle is often political pressure and a culture that tolerates some unethical practices.

nonprofit.title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesian Governance
nonprofit.short_title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesi…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how ethics, accountability, and transparency work together in Indonesian government systems. It found that even with digitalization efforts, if there isn't a strong enough foundation of ethics, these measures can fail to prevent corruption and lose public trust. The research suggests integrating ethical practices, making information transparent, and ensuring accountability are all important for effective governance. By combining these elements, Indonesia can improve its government systems and build more trustworthy relationships with the people it serves.
